obligations.text: No attempt of a `liveRun` is handed to a host backend unless its full worst-case exposure, from the backend's declared cost model and bound, is durably reserved in the journal first and fits both the run cap and the journal's cap; a binding whose cost model is `unknown`, or that has no entry in the live configuration, is refused before the journal is opened.

Cancellation by `AbortSignal`, the run deadline or `shutdown` never releases a reservation for an attempt that was handed to a host backend and has not settled; its charge stays liability in the journal, its item is `interrupted`, and a late Promise settlement is discarded and never settles the ticket.

For the same inputs, scripted backends and clock, `liveRun` writes the same documents, bytes, status and exit code as `rustev_live::run` called from Rust, and the binding adds no authority: its authorizer is 043 3.12's declarative rule list, and no binding value is a permission.

A journal created by a live run records a stable `journal_id` and `created_at_ms` in its header, and every `rustev.live-run/1` names the journal's id, creation time, whether this run created it, and the cumulative spend before the run, so a run that started its cumulative cap at zero on a new file is visible and never silent.
Every test and conformance case of this spec uses scripted host backends and a temporary `testing` journal; no CI job makes a live or paid provider call, and the WebAssembly package gains nothing.

sectionHeadings: 067: Node binding: live repeat runs over host backends (amends 027, 043 and 063)
3.4 The journal and the output directory are file paths
record.summary: A proposed amendment of approved specs 063 (3.9), 027 (3.3, 3.7) and 043 (section 2, 3.2.2), for release 0.5.1 (#539). A Node host whose model backends are TypeScript `DecisionBackend`s (027 3.6) cannot run fresh repeat runs of its plans through Rustev: the binding's repeat commands refuse the `live` source (063 3.9.4), and `rustev eval live` links only the rules backend (043 3.13.2). So the host keeps its own harness, outside Rustev's spend journal and caps. This spec adds `engine.liveRun`, an asynchronous method over `rustev_live::run` with the CLI's inputs, the engine's registered host backends and the same documents as `rustev eval live`, all or none for the final files. The journal is a file path the binding opens under 043 3.5's lock and durability rules, and no attempt is sent before its full worst-case exposure is durably reserved. A host backend's exposure is the cost model and bound it already declares (027 3.6.1); an `unknown` model is refused. Probe-only, resume and rerun-interrupted are 043's; an `AbortSignal` or `shutdown` ends the run `interrupted` with every reserved, unsettled attempt kept as liability. The cumulative cap holds per journal file, so CI must persist the file; a journal created by a run records an id and creation time, and the run report names them, so a fresh journal is visible, never silent. Tests use scripted host backends only; CI makes no live or paid call. This fulfills 043 section 2's "the Node binding exposes it in its own spec".
